You are rapid_thistle87, one of 10 agents working together on the same task on a shared platform. All
10 agents form one group, and you work with brisk_harbor75, early_island22, gentle_otter27, jolly_ember22, pale_kettle84, pale_lantern48, sandy_walnut42, urban_comet97, zesty_lantern63. Each agent works in its own sandbox, on its
own git repository. Your group shares one `main` branch, which every member can push to, and one channel
(`group`). Work together with your teammates to make your group's `main` as good as possible. Use `group` to
coordinate and share helpful findings.

## Setting
Your task is to recreate a program from scratch based only on its observable behavior and bundled documentation.
You are given a reference executable and its documentation.
Treat the reference executable as a specification you can query through its normal user interface.

Your submission must be an independent implementation.
Using the original source code, wrapping the reference executable, or installing an existing implementation does not satisfy the task and will receive no credit.
It will be detected by an automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

<RULES>
## What is NOT allowed

### 1. Using an existing implementation

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the reference executable

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `/opt/reference/executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the reference executable (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that only runs `chmod +x ./executable` or copies the reference executable (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. How the reference executable may be observed

All information about the reference `/opt/reference/executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `/opt/reference/executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `/opt/reference/executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the reference `/opt/reference/executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

## Your repository and your group's main
- In your sandbox, `/workspace` is your own git repository, and the reference executable is in `/opt/reference`. No one else can see it.
- Your group's shared `main` is the remote `team`. Fetch it with `git fetch team` (you get `team/main`),
  and push to it with `git push team HEAD:main`. **Your local files do not update automatically when a
  teammate pushes.**
- A push must be a fast-forward: if `main` has moved since you last fetched, the push is rejected. Fetch,
  merge `team/main` into your work, and push again.
- When you push, the platform posts in `group` on your behalf, with your commit message, a summary of the
  changed files, and a pointer to the new `main`. Write commit messages that say what changed.
- Your git name and email are preconfigured as your agent name. Do not change them.
- Commit with `git commit -m "<message>"`: there is no editor in the sandbox, so a commit without `-m`
  fails with an empty message.
- Run the reference executable and your experiments outside `/workspace` (for example in `/tmp`), so that they do not change your
  repository.

## Scoring rule
Your payoff is your group's final score: the fraction of hidden tests passed by the code on `main` at
the end. Every agent receives the same payoff.
- **Only the code on your group's `main` at the end is graded.** Code in your own repository, or shared
  through pointers, does not count until it is pushed to `main`. If no one pushes, the initial commit is
  graded.
- Everyone keeps working until time runs out.

## Platform
The platform is the shared place where agents announce what they are exploring, building, or have found,
and ask each other questions. Typical posts include a direction you are exploring, a component you are
building, a finding (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case), a proposal for how to organize the work, or a question.
- `post` publishes a message to `group`, with a title: a one-line summary of the message, up
  to 120 characters. Every post gets a number. Mention someone with @name.
- To share code, commit it, then list it in the post's `attach`. The platform adds a pointer
  (`[[<sha>:<path>#La-b]]`) to the post for each item. `attach` can name:
  - `path#La-b`: a file in your `HEAD`, optionally with a line range;
  - `<sha>:path#La-b`: a file in another commit;
  - a commit's sha, or `HEAD`: a whole commit;
  - `file:<path>#La-b`: the current content of a single file, even if it is not committed. Readers see
    only that file.
  Pointing at a commit makes all files in that commit readable. Uncommitted changes are not shared.
- `read_feed` lists the new posts in `group`, and any unopened posts that mention you, one line each
  (number, author, channel, title). `read_feed` with a post's number shows its full text, with its
  pointers expanded into the code and a diff against your own version.
- You can fetch any code shared with you into your repository with `git fetch origin` (as
  `origin/shared/<author>/<sha>`), and then merge or cherry-pick what you want.

After each action, a platform notice lists the new posts on the channels you can read, one line each (number,
author, channel, title, and a marker when the post carries code). A post that mentions you appears in
every notice until you open it with `read_feed` and its number.

## Working together
- Start by **getting an overview of what the reference program supports**, enough to understand how the
  program should behave in its main cases, and share it in `group` as a list (if a teammate has
  already posted one, add to theirs), so the group can keep extending the plan and everyone stays up
  to date on which areas are covered. Then **agree with your teammates on how to work together**:
  split the work, or have several members build the same part and compare, keeping the best of each.
  If parts depend on each other, agree on the interfaces first, and while you wait for a part you
  need, write tests for it with expected output from the reference program.
- If a teammate has already posted a plan, **follow it and propose changes to it** instead of posting
  a competing one.
- Work in a cycle: (1) pick an area and say so in `group`; (2) build it on top of the latest `main`;
  (3) compare its output with the reference program on the same inputs; (4) commit, `git fetch team`, merge
  `team/main`, and `git push team HEAD:main`; (5) post what you finished, with a pointer, then go back
  to (1). Report a part as done only once it is on `main`: a part that is not on `main` does not count.
- Passing your own tests does not mean the task is done: always assume the hidden tests cover more
  than your tests do. **When your tests all pass, test more areas.** Add cases for features and
  options your tests do not cover yet, including the parts your teammates are handling. A new area
  usually matters more than more cases in an area that already works.
- **Never stop calling tool before time is up. When you are not sure what to do next, review the
  whole program on `main` again** as a reviewer looking for bugs: features of the reference program that
  are missing or only partly handled, edge cases (empty input, `null`, deep nesting, large numbers,
  unusual option combinations), and error paths. Do not review only your own part: test the whole
  program, including your teammates' parts, with inputs you have not tried yet. Test each suspicion
  against the reference program, and fix what differs.
- **If one approach keeps failing, change the approach instead of retrying it.** Post in `group` what
  you tried, so teammates do not repeat it and can suggest other ideas. If you are still stuck, put a
  version that handles the common cases on `main` for now, and come back to it later.
- Do not leave hard parts as known gaps. Come back to them, discuss them with your teammates, and solve as
  many of them as possible: **keep improving `main` until time runs out.**

lla

Modern, customizable, feature-rich and extensible `ls` replacement.
Documentation · Features · Installation · Display Formats · Command Reference

## Overview lla is a modern `ls` replacement that transforms how developers interact with their filesystem. Built with Rust's performance capabilities and designed with user experience in mind, lla combines the familiarity of `ls` with powerful features like specialized views, Git integration, and a robust plugin system with an extensible list of plugins to add more functionality. ## Features - Multiple Views: Default clean view, long format, tree structure, table layout, grid display - Diff Command: Human-friendly directory or file comparisons (local ↔ local or git) with size/line deltas and unified diff output - Git Integration: Built-in status visualization and repository insights - Advanced Organization: Timeline view, storage analysis, recursive exploration - Smart Navigation: Interactive directory jumper with bookmarks and history - Smart Search: complex filtering patterns (OR, AND, NOT, XOR), regex support, content search - Customization: Plugin system, theme manager, custom shortcuts, configurable display - High Performance: Built with Rust, modern UI, clean listings - Smart Sorting: Multiple criteria, directory-first option, natural sorting - Flexible Config: Easy initialization, plugin management, configuration tools - Rich Plugin Ecosystem: File ops and metadata enhancements, code analysis, git tools, and more - Smart Filters: Range-based size/time filters, reusable presets, cache-aware refinements - Git-aware Filtering: Optional `.gitignore` support via `--respect-gitignore` or config defaults ## Installation ### Using Installation Script The easiest way to install lla is using our installation script: ```bash curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chaqchase/lla/main/install.sh | bash ``` This script will automatically: - Detect your OS and architecture - Download the appropriate binary - Verify the checksum - Install lla to `/usr/local/bin` ### Using Package Manager | Package Manager / Platform | Command | | -------------------------- | ------------------- | | Cargo | `cargo install lla` | | macOS (Homebrew) | `brew install lla` | | Arch Linux (paru) | `paru -S lla` | | NetBSD (pkgin) | `pkgin install lla` | | X-CMD | `x install lla` | ### Manual Installation ```bash # Manual - Example is for amd64 GNU, replaces the file names if downloading for a different arch. wget -c https://github.com/chaqchase/lla/releases/download//-> -O lla # Example /v0.3.9/lla-linux-amd64 sudo chmod +x lla sudo chown root:root lla sudo mv lla /usr/local/bin/lla ``` ### Upgrading Upgrade to the latest (or a specific) release without leaving the terminal: ```bash # Upgrade to the latest release (auto-detects OS/arch, verifies checksums) lla upgrade # Target a specific tag or custom installation path lla upgrade --version v0.5.1 --path /usr/local/bin/lla ``` The upgrade command reuses the official install script logic, renders animated progress indicators, verifies the `SHA256SUMS` manifest, and atomically swaps the `lla` binary in place (defaults to the path of the running executable—override with `--path` if needed). ### Post Installation After installation, initialize your setup: ```bash # Guided setup with theme/format wizard (default) lla init # Write the default config without prompts lla init --default # View your config lla config ``` The revamped wizard (now the default) walks you through: - Look & feel choices (icons, theme, default view, permission format) - Listing defaults (sort order, directory inclusion, depth limits) - Sorting & filtering toggles (dirs-first, natural sort, dotfile visibility, case sensitivity) - Long-view behavior (relative dates, hide group column, column selection) - Plugin directory selection, plugin enablement, and recursion safety limits ## Display Formats ### Core Views #### Default View Clean, distraction-free listing for quick directory scans: ```bash lla ``` #### Long Format Rich metadata display for detailed file analysis: ```bash lla -l ``` Options and tweaks: - Hide the group column (useful on single-user systems): ```bash lla -l --hide-group ``` - Show relative dates (e.g., "2h ago"): ```bash lla -l --relative-dates ``` To make these defaults, add to your config (`~/.config/lla/config.toml`): ```toml [formatters.long] hide_group = true relative_dates = true columns = ["permissions", "size", "modified", "user", "group", "name", "field:git_status", "field:tags"] ``` The `columns` array lets you control the precise column order. Use built-in keys (`permissions`, `size`, `modified`, `user`, `group`, `name`, `path`, `plugins`) or reference any plugin-provided field with the `field:` prefix (e.g., `field:git_status`, `field:complexity_score`). #### Tree Structure Hierarchical exploration of directory relationships: ```bash lla -t -d 3 # Navigate up to 3 levels deep ``` #### Archive Introspection List archive contents as a virtual directory (no extraction). Supported: `.zip`, `.tar`, `.tar.gz`, `.tgz`. ``` lla my_archive.zip -t # tree view lla project.tar.gz -l # long view lla my_archive.tgz --json lla my_archive.zip -l -f ".rs" # filter by extension on internal paths ``` #### Single-file Listing You can pass a single file path to list it directly with any view or machine output: ``` lla README.md # default view lla Cargo.toml -l # long view lla src/main.rs --json # machine output ``` ### Enhanced Organization #### Table Layout Structured view optimized for data comparison: ```bash lla -T ``` The `[formatters.table].columns` setting mirrors the long-view syntax, so you can mix built-in fields with plugin-provided metadata: ```toml [formatters.table] columns = ["permissions", "size", "modified", "name", "field:git_branch", "field:git_commit"] ``` #### Diff View (Files & Directories) Compare directories or individual files (including against git references) with compact, colorized summaries. Directory comparisons still show the status table with size deltas, while file comparisons add a unified diff plus size/line-change stats: ```bash lla diff src ../backup/src lla diff apps/api --git # compare working tree vs HEAD lla diff src --git --git-ref HEAD~1 # compare against another commit lla diff Cargo.lock ../backup/Cargo.lock lla diff Cargo.lock --git --git-ref HEAD~1 ``` For directories, the diff view groups entries by status, colors the change indicator, and shows left/right sizes plus the net delta so you can spot growth at a glance. For files, lla prints a size summary, line-count delta, and a git-style unified diff (with automatic binary detection so unreadable data isn’t dumped to your terminal). #### Grid Display Space-efficient layout for dense directories: ```bash lla -g # Basic grid view lla -g --grid-ignore # Grid view ignoring terminal width (Warning: may extend beyond screen) ``` Note: Grid output no longer appends a trailing blank newline. ### Specialized Views #### Git Integration Smart repository insights: ```bash lla -G ``` #### Timeline Organization Chronological file tracking: ```bash lla --timeline ``` #### Storage Analysis Visual disk usage insights, including a total size summary: ```bash lla -S # use --include-dirs to calculate directory sizes (recursive; slower on large trees) ``` ### Advanced Navigation #### Jump-to-Directory (Interactive Directory Jumper) Quickly navigate to bookmarked or recently visited directories with an interactive keyboard-driven prompt: ```bash # One-time setup for seamless directory jumping lla jump --setup # Interactive directory selection lla jump # Add directory to bookmarks lla jump --add ~/projects/my-app # Remove bookmark lla jump --remove ~/projects/my-app # List all bookmarks and recent history lla jump --list # Clear history lla jump --clear-history ``` **Features:** - **Interactive Selection**: Arrow keys and Enter to select from bookmarked and recent directories - **Smart History**: Automatically records directory visits (respects `exclude_paths`) - **Bookmarks**: Add favorite directories for quick access - **Deduplication**: No duplicate entries in history - **Shell Integration**: Works seamlessly with shell commands like `cd` **How it works:** 1. Bookmarks (marked with ★) appear first in the selection list 2. Recent directories follow, showing directory name and full path 3. Use arrow keys to navigate, Enter to select 4. The selected path is printed to stdout for shell integration 5. History is automatically maintained as you navigate directories **Shell Integration Setup:** Since `lla` runs as a child process, it cannot directly change your shell's working directory. To enable seamless directory jumping, run the automatic setup: ```bash lla jump --setup ``` This will automatically detect your shell (bash, zsh, or fish) and add the necessary function to your shell configuration file. After setup, restart your terminal or run `source ~/.zshrc` (or equivalent for your shell). Then use `j` to jump to directories interactively! **Examples:** ```bash # One-time setup (auto-detects your shell) lla jump --setup # shell override lla jump --setup --shell fish # Navigate to a frequently used directory (after setup) j # Add your project directories to bookmarks lla jump --add ~/dev/my-project lla jump --add ~/work/client-app lla jump --add ~/personal/blog # View all your saved locations lla jump --list ``` #### Fuzzy Search (Experimental) Interactive file discovery with multi-select and batch actions: ```bash lla --fuzzy ``` Keyboard shortcuts: - Ctrl+J / Ctrl+K: move down / up - Ctrl+N / Ctrl+P: move down / up - Ctrl+D / Ctrl+U: half-page down / up - Ctrl+G: jump to end - Ctrl+Shift+G: jump to start - Ctrl+C / Esc: exit - Space: toggle select - Enter: confirm (returns the highlighted file or all selected files) - Ctrl+E: open selected file(s) in your editor - Ctrl+Y: copy selected path(s) to clipboard - Ctrl+O: open selected file(s) with the system opener (open/xdg-open/start) - F2: rename the highlighted file (Enter: confirm, Esc/Ctrl+C: cancel) Search input shortcuts: - Ctrl+W: delete word backward - Ctrl+H: delete character (backspace) - Ctrl+A: jump to start of input (`Home` also works) - End: jump to end of input Editor selection (for `Ctrl+E`): - Config override: `listers.fuzzy.editor` (takes priority) - Environment: `$EDITOR`, then `$VISUAL` - Fallback: `nano` (macOS/Linux) or `notepad` (Windows) Example config: ```toml [listers.fuzzy] editor = "nvim" # or: "code --wait" ``` Tip: for GUI editors, configure a “wait” flag so lla returns after you close the file, e.g. `code --wait` or `subl -w`. #### Deep Directory Exploration (Recursive) Comprehensive subdirectory listing: ```bash lla -R lla -R -d 3 # Set exploration depth ``` The `-R` option can be integrated with other options to create a more specific view. # lla Themes

lla provides a powerful and flexible theming system that allows you to customize the appearance of your file listings. Each theme is defined in a TOML file and can customize colors for files, folders, permissions, and more.

lla ships with a default theme collection, you can pull all builtin themes with the following command:

```bash
lla theme pull # pull all builtin themes
```

you can also install custom themes using the following command:

```bash
lla theme install /path/to/theme.toml
# or a directory with multiple themes
lla theme install /path/to/themes/
```

## Table of Contents

- [Theme Location](#theme-location)
- [Theme Structure](#theme-structure)
- [Color Formats](#color-formats)
- [Basic Elements](#basic-elements)
- [Special Files](#special-files)
- [Extension System](#extension-system)
- [Built-in Themes](#built-in-themes)
- [Usage](#usage)

## Theme Location

Themes are stored in `~/.config/lla/themes/` with a `.toml` extension:

```
~/.config/lla/themes/
├── dark.toml
├── light.toml
├── poimandres.toml
└── custom.toml
```

## Theme Structure

A theme file has the following main sections:

```toml
# Theme metadata
name = "my_theme"
author = "Your Name"
description = "A description of your theme"

# Core colors for basic elements
[colors]
file = "#FFFFFF"
directory = "#89AFFF"
...

# Special file rules
[special_files]
...

# Extension-based colors
[extensions]
...
```

## Color Formats

lla supports multiple color formats for maximum flexibility:

```toml
[colors]
# 1. Named Colors (Basic terminal colors)
file = "white"
directory = "blue"
symlink = "bright_cyan"

# 2. RGB Format
file = { r = 255, g = 255, b = 255 }
directory = { r = 81, g = 154, b = 255 }

# 3. Hex Format
file = "#FFFFFF"              # 6-digit hex
directory = "#89F"           # 3-digit hex
symlink = "#89DBFFFF"       # 8-digit hex (alpha ignored)

# 4. HSL Format (h: 0-360, s: 0-1, l: 0-1)
directory = { h = 180, s = 0.5, l = 0.6 }

# 5. No Color
disabled = "none"
```

### Available Named Colors

Basic Colors:

- `black`, `red`, `green`, `yellow`, `blue`, `magenta`, `cyan`, `white`

Bright Variants:

- `bright_black` (or `gray`/`grey`)
- `bright_red`, `bright_green`, `bright_yellow`
- `bright_blue`, `bright_magenta`, `bright_cyan`, `bright_white`

Additional Colors:

- `navy`, `teal`, `maroon`, `purple`, `olive`, `silver`

## Basic Elements

The `[colors]` section defines the core colors:

```toml
[colors]
# Core UI Elements
file = "#FFFFFF"        # Regular files
directory = "#89AFFF"   # Directories
symlink = "#89DBFF"     # Symbolic links
executable = "#5DE4B3"  # Executable files

# Metadata
size = "#5DE4B3"       # File sizes
date = "#FCBCFA"       # Timestamps
user = "#D0679D"       # User names
group = "#8A9092"      # Group names

# Permissions
permission_dir = "#89AFFF"   # Directory permission
permission_read = "#5DE4B3"  # Read permission
permission_write = "#FFFFC2" # Write permission
permission_exec = "#D0679D"  # …349 tokens truncated… colors for groups
[extensions.colors]
```

## Color Resolution Order

When determining a file's color, lla follows this priority:

1. If it's a directory:

   - Exact folder name match
   - Folder pattern match
   - Default directory color

2. If it's a file:
   - Exact filename match
   - Dotfile match
   - Pattern match
   - Extension-specific color
   - Extension group color
   - Default file color

## Built-in Themes

lla includes several pre-configured themes:

- **default**: Traditional terminal colors with carefully selected colors for optimal visibility
- **dark**: Modern dark theme with enhanced visibility and rich colors for dark terminals
- **light**: Clean theme optimized for light terminals with maximum readability
- **ayu_dark**: Dark theme inspired by the Ayu Dark color scheme, featuring deep backgrounds and vibrant accents
- **ayu_light**: Light theme with carefully selected colors for optimal readability
- **ayu_mirage**: Refined dark theme with muted colors and soft contrasts
- **catppuccin_mocha**: A soothing pastel theme for the high-spirited, featuring warm, cozy colors
- **circuit_dreams**: A theme inspired by vintage circuit boards and electronic components
- **cosmic_night**: A sophisticated dark theme with cosmic-inspired colors and nebula accents
- **deep_sea**: An ocean-inspired theme featuring the colors of marine depths
- **dracula**: Classic Dracula color scheme with vibrant colors and high contrast
- **forest_depths**: A theme inspired by the depths of an ancient forest at twilight
- **gruvbox_dark**: Retro groove color scheme with warm, earthy tones and high contrast
- **material_ocean**: Deep blue theme based on Material Design, featuring oceanic colors
- **moonlight**: A minimal theme with subtle blue-gray tones inspired by moonlit nights
- **neon_dreams**: A vibrant cyberpunk theme featuring electric neons and digital gradients
- **nord**: Arctic, north-bluish color palette with elegant pastel colors
- **one_dark**: Dark theme inspired by Atom, featuring a perfect balance of cool and warm colors
- **poimandres**: Deep space aesthetic with vibrant accents
- **synthwave_84**: A retro-computing theme inspired by 1980s aesthetics
- **tokyo_night**: Dark theme inspired by the vibrant lights of Tokyo at night
- **vesper**: Minimalist dark theme with warm accents
- **zen**: A minimal monochromatic theme emphasizing simplicity and clarity

## Usage

Set your theme in `~/.config/lla/config.toml`:

```toml
theme = "dark"  # Without .toml extension
```

Or use the command line:

```bash
lla config --set theme dark
```

To disable colors:

```bash
lla config --set theme none
```

or if you don't want any colors you can add "--no-colors" flag to lla:

```bash
lla --no-colors # works with all listing commands
```

content.text: Theme installation is a distinct uncovered path with deterministic behavior: it copies `.toml` files into `~/.config/lla/themes` and prints a count. I’m implementing that subcommand as an isolated helper so the CLI owner can dispatch it cleanly.

const patch="*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /workspace/theme_cmd.py
+"""Small implementation of lla's non-interactive theme install command."""
+import os
+import shutil
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+def install(path: str) -> int:
+    source = Path(path).expanduser()
+    if not source.exists():
+        print(f"\n✗ Error\n\n  Path does not exist: {path}\n")
+        return 1
+    if source.is_file():
+        files = [source]
+    elif source.is_dir():
+        files = sorted(source.glob("*.toml"), key=lambda p: p.name)
+    else:
+        files = []
+    if not files:
+        print("\n✗ Error\n\n  No theme files found in the specified path\n")
+        return 1
+    dest = Path.home() / ".config" / "lla" / "themes"
+    dest.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    for file in files:
+        shutil.copy2(file, dest / file.name)
+        print(f"✓ Installed theme: {file.name}")
+    print(f"\n{len(files)} theme(s) installed successfully!\nUse lla theme to select a theme")
+    return 0
+
+
+def run(args):
+    if len(args) >= 2 and args[0] == "theme" and args[1] == "install":
+        if len(args) < 3:
+            print("error: The following required arguments were not provided:\n    <path>")
+            return 2
+        return install(args[2])
+    return None
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(install(sys.argv[1]))
*** End Patch";
const r=await tools.apply_patch(patch); text(r)

from pathlib import Path

INSTALL_HELP = """executable-install 
Install a plugin

USAGE:
    executable install [OPTIONS]

OPTIONS:
        --dir <dir>    Install a plugin from a local directory
        --git <git>    Install a plugin from a GitHub repository URL
    -h, --help         Print help information
        --prebuilt     Install plugins from the latest prebuilt release (default)
"""
UPDATE_HELP = """executable-update
Update installed plugins

USAGE:
    executable update [name]

ARGS:
    <name>    Name of the plugin to update (updates all if not specified)

OPTIONS:
    -h, --help    Print help information
"""
UPGRADE_HELP = """executable-upgrade
Upgrade the lla CLI to the latest (or specified) release

USAGE:
    executable upgrade [OPTIONS]

OPTIONS:
    -h, --help                 Print help information
        --path <path>          Install location for the lla binary (defaults to the current
                               executable path)
    -v, --version <version>    Upgrade to a specific release tag (defaults to the latest release)
"""


def run(argv):
    """Handle commands whose normal successful path requires network access."""
    if not argv or argv[0] not in ("install", "update", "upgrade"):
        return False
    cmd, args = argv[0], argv[1:]
    if "--help" in args or "-h" in args:
        print({"install": INSTALL_HELP, "update": UPDATE_HELP, "upgrade": UPGRADE_HELP}[cmd])
        return True
    if cmd == "update":
        print("\n✗ Plugin Error\n\n  No plugins are currently installed\n")
    elif cmd == "install":
        if "--dir" in args:
            i = args.index("--dir")
            value = args[i + 1] if i + 1 < len(args) else ""
            if not Path(value).is_dir():
                print("╭─ lla ────────────────╮\n│   Local Installation │\n╰──────────────────────╯\n\n╭─ Source ──────────────────╮\n│   Directory  │  %s │\n╰───────────────────────────╯\n\n\n✗ Plugin Error\n\n  Directory not found: %s\n" % (value, value))
            else:
                print("\n✗ Plugin Error\n\n  No valid plugin found in directory\n")
        else:
            print("\n✗ Plugin Error\n\n  Network access is unavailable\n")
    else:
        print("\n✗ Upgrade Error\n\n  Network access is unavailable\n")

"""Plugin related CLI commands for lla."""
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path


LIST_HELP = """executable-list-plugins 
List all available plugins

USAGE:
    executable list-plugins

OPTIONS:
    -h, --help    Print help information
"""

PLUGIN_HELP = """executable-plugin 
Run a plugin action

USAGE:
    executable plugin [OPTIONS] [--] [ARGS]

ARGS:
    <plugin_name>       Name of the plugin
    <plugin_action>     Action to perform
    <plugin_args>...    Arguments for the plugin action

OPTIONS:
    -a, --action <action>    Action to perform (alternative to positional)
    -h, --help               Print help information
    -n, --name <name>        Name of the plugin (alternative to positional)
    -r, --args <args>...     Arguments for the plugin action (alternative to positional)
"""


def _plugin_dir():
    # Match the documented default; installed plugins are shared objects.
    cfg = Path.home() / ".config/lla/config.toml"
    try:
        import re
        txt = cfg.read_text()
        m = re.search(r'(?m)^plugins_dir\s*=\s*["\']([^"\']+)', txt)
        if m:
            return Path(os.path.expanduser(m.group(1)))
    except OSError:
        pass
    return Path.home() / ".config/lla/plugins"


def _libraries():
    """Return loadable ELF candidates and loader diagnostics."""
    found, warnings = [], []
    try:
        entries = _plugin_dir().iterdir()
    except OSError:
        return found, warnings
    for p in entries:
        if not p.is_file() or p.suffix.lower() not in (".so", ".dll", ".dylib"):
            continue
        try:
            magic = p.open("rb").read(4)
        except OSError:
            continue
        if magic == b"\x7fELF":
            found.append(p.stem)
        else:
            warnings.append(f'⚠️ Failed to load plugin library "{p}": {p}: file too short')
    return found, warnings


def run(args):
    """Dispatch plugin subcommands; return True if consumed."""
    if not args or args[0] not in ("plugin", "list-plugins"):
        return False
    cmd, rest = args[0], args[1:]
    if cmd == "list-plugins":
        if any(a in ("-h", "--help") for a in rest):
            print(LIST_HELP)
        else:
            found, warnings = _libraries()

const patch="*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /workspace/config_cmd.py
+"""Common non-interactive config and init commands."""
+import os, re
+from pathlib import Path
+
+CONFIG_HELP = '''executable-config 
+View or modify configuration
+
+USAGE:
+    executable config [OPTIONS] [SUBCOMMAND]
+
+OPTIONS:
+    -h, --help                 Print help information
+        --set <KEY> <VALUE>    Set a configuration value (e.g., --set plugins_dir /new/path)
+
+SUBCOMMANDS:
+    diff              Compare config overrides against defaults
+    help              Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)
+    show-effective    Show the merged config (global + nearest .lla.toml)
+'''
+
+def config_path():
+    return Path.home()/'.config'/'lla'/'config.toml'
+
+def _effective():
+    p=config_path()
+    plugins=str(Path.home()/'.config'/'lla'/'plugins')
+    txt=p.read_text(errors='replace') if p.exists() else ''
+    m=re.search(r'(?m)^plugins_dir\s*=\s*["\']([^"\']+)',txt)
+    if m: plugins=os.path.expanduser(m.group(1))
+    return f'''Profile overlay: <none>
+default_sort = "name"
+default_format = "default"
+enabled_plugins = []
+plugins_dir = "{plugins}"
+exclude_paths = []
+default_depth = 3
+show_icons = false
+include_dirs = false
+theme = "default"
+permission_format = "symbolic"
+
+[sort]
+dirs_first = false
+case_sensitive = false
+natural = true
+
+[filter]
+case_sensitive = false
+no_dotfiles = false
+respect_gitignore = false
+
+[filter.presets]
+
+[formatters.tree]
+max_lines = 20000
+
+[formatters.grid]
+ignore_width = false
+max_width = 200
+
+[formatters.long]
+hide_group = false
+relative_dates = false
+columns = [
+    "permissions",
+    "size",
+    "modified",
+    "user",
+    "group",
+    "name",
+]
+
+[formatters.table]
+columns = [
+    "permissions",
+    "size",
+    "modified",
+    "name",
+]
+
+[formatters.sizemap]
+
+[listers.recursive]
+max_entries = 20000
+
+[listers.fuzzy]
+ignore_patterns = [
+    "node_modules",
+    "target",
+    ".git",
+    ".idea",
+    ".vscode",
+]
+editor = ""
+
+[shortcuts]
+
+[plugin_aliases]'''
+
+def run(argv):
+    if not argv: return False
+    if argv[0]=='init':
+        if '--help' in argv or '-h' in argv:
+            print('executable-init \nInitialize the configuration file\n\nUSAGE:\n    executable init [OPTIONS]\n\nOPTIONS:\n        --default    Write the default config without launching the wizard\n    -h, --help       Print help information'); return True
+        p=config_path(); p.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
+        if not p.exists(): p.write_text('default_sort = "name"\ndefault_format = "default"\n')
+        print(f'Config file already exists at "{p}"\nUse `lla config` to view or modify the configuration.')
+        return True
+    if argv[0]!='config': return False
+    a=argv[1:]
+    if not a or a[0] in ('--help','-h','help'):
+        if '--set' in a: pass
+        else: print(CONFIG_HELP,end=''); return True
+    if a[0]=='show-effective': print(_effective()); return True
+    if a[:2]==['diff','--default']:
+        print('No configuration overrides found.'); return True
+    if '--set' in a:
+        i=a.index('--set')
+        if len(a)<i+3: print('error: The following required arguments were not provided:\n    <KEY> <VALUE>'); return True
+        key,val=a[i+1:i+3]
+        if key not in ('default_sort','default_format','enabled_plugins','plugins_dir','exclude_paths','default_depth','show_icons','include_dirs','theme','permission_format'):
+            print(f'\n✗ Config Error\n\n  {key}: unknown configuration key: {key}\n'); return True
+        p=config_path(); p.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
+        txt=p.read_text() if p.exists() else ''
+        if re.search(r'(?m)^'+re.escape(key)+r'\s*=',txt): txt=re.sub(r'(?m)^'+re.escape(key)+r'\s*=.*$',f'{key} = "{val}"',txt)
+        else: txt+=f'\n{key} = "{val}"\n'
+        p.write_text(txt); print(f'Updated {key} = {val}'); return True
+    print(CONFIG_HELP,end=''); return True
*** End Patch";
const r=await tools.apply_patch(patch); text(r)

"""Read-only metadata view for ZIP and tar archives."""
import os, stat, tarfile, zipfile, pwd, grp
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import PurePosixPath

def archive_records(filename, recursive=False):
    low=filename.lower()
    if not low.endswith(('.zip','.tar','.tar.gz','.tgz')): return None
    source=os.path.abspath(filename)
    members=[]
    try:
        if zipfile.is_zipfile(filename):
            with zipfile.ZipFile(filename) as z:
                for i in z.infolist():
                    name=i.filename.rstrip('/')
                    if not name: continue
                    mode=(i.external_attr >> 16) & 0xffff
                    isdir=i.is_dir() or stat.S_ISDIR(mode)
                    if not mode: mode=0o755 if isdir else 0o600
                    # lla reports ZIP entries without a usable Unix timestamp as epoch.
                    ts='1970-01-01T00:00:00Z'
                    members.append((name,'dir' if isdir else 'file',0 if isdir else i.file_size,mode,ts,'root','root',None))
        else:
            with tarfile.open(filename,'r:*') as t:
                for i in t.getmembers():
                    name=i.name.rstrip('/')
                    if not name: continue
                    typ='dir' if i.isdir() else ('symlink' if i.issym() else ('file' if i.isfile() else 'other'))
                    ts=datetime.fromtimestamp(i.mtime,timezone.utc).strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')
                    try: user=pwd.getpwuid(i.uid).pw_name
                    except Exception: user=str(i.uid)
                    try: group=grp.getgrgid(i.gid).gr_name
                    except Exception: group=str(i.gid)
                    target=i.linkname if typ=='symlink' else None
                    members.append((name,typ,0 if typ=='dir' else i.size,i.mode,ts,user,group,target))
    except (OSError,tarfile.TarError,zipfile.BadZipFile): return None
    known={m[0]:m for m in members}; explicit_names=set(known); directories=set()
    for name,*_ in members:
        parts=PurePosixPath(name).parts
        for n in range(1,len(parts)):
            d='/'.join(parts[:n]); directories.add(d)
    for d in directories:
        if d not in known: known[d]=(d,'dir',0,0o755,'1970-01-01T00:00:00Z','root','root',None)
    selected=[]
    for name,item in known.items():
        if recursive or '/' not in name: selected.append(item)
    out=[]
    for name,typ,size,mode,modified,user,group,target in selected:
        basename=name.rsplit('/',1)[-1]
        ext=os.path.splitext(basename)[1][1:] or None
        out.append({'path':os.path.basename(filename)+'/'+name,'name':basename,'extension':ext,'file_type':typ,
          'size_bytes':size,'modified':modified,'created':None,'accessed':None,'mode_octal':f'{mode & 0o7777:04o}',
          'owner_user':user,'owner_group':group,'inode':None,'hard_links':None,'symlink_target':target,
          'is_hidden':basename.startswith('.'),'git_status':None,'plugin':({'archive_source':source} if name in explicit_names else {})})
    return out
"}

def format_permissions(mode: int, fmt: str = "symbolic") -> str:
    """Format an st_mode value using the CLI's permission-format names."""
    kind = file_type(mode)
    bits = mode & 0o777
    octal = f"{bits:03o}"
    if fmt == "compact":
        return octal
    if fmt == "octal":
        return type_char(mode) + octal
    if fmt == "binary":
        return type_char(mode) + f"{bits:09b}"
    if fmt == "verbose":
        def triplet(value: int) -> str:
            return "".join(c if value & bit else "-" for c, bit in (("r", 4), ("w", 2), ("x", 1)))
        return f"type:{kind} owner:{triplet((bits >> 6) & 7)} group:{triplet((bits >> 3) & 7)} others:{triplet(bits & 7)}"
    chars = "".join(c if bits & bit else "-" for bit, c in (
        (0o400, "r"), (0o200, "w"), (0o100, "x"),
        (0o040, "r"), (0o020, "w"), (0o010, "x"),
        (0o004, "r"), (0o002, "w"), (0o001, "x")))
    return (type_char(mode) + chars) * 3
